#6833. Willy Chavarria Is Honored at the 6th Annual We Are All Human Gala

Plus, special recognition for Dolores Huerta and Mark D. Levine and a Cirque du Soleil performance.

Last night at Cipriani Wall Street, the sixth annual We Are All Human Gala celebrated the advancement of the Latin community. “Latinos are prosperity, power, and progress, but the stereotypes, the biases, and the negative narratives have not disappeared,” Claudia Romo Edelman, founder and executive chair of We Are All Human, said in her opening remarks. “That’s why this moment matters, because we have many Latino moments that we together can turn into momentum, and use that momentum to change our perception for good, once and for all.”

We Are All Human, through its Hispanic Star initiative, is a nonprofit aimed at uplifting Hispanics in economic and cultural spaces. According to its website, “Hispanic Star seeks to reframe Hispanics not merely as a fast-growing demographic, but as a vital economic, cultural, and civic force shaping the United States’ future.”

Throughout the evening, many leaders were recognized for their contributions to society. These included fashion designer Willy Chavarria, CEO and creative director of Willy Chavarria; Mark D. Levine, New York City comptroller; Bea Perez, executive vice president and global chief communications, sustainability, and strategic partnerships officer at The Coca-Cola Company, and chair of The Coca-Cola Foundation; and Henry R. Muñoz III, American activist and founder and CEO of Cultural Productions.

“For generations, our people have been told where we can go, how far we can rise, and which doors we’re allowed to walk through on our own land,” Chavarria said in his speech. “Now, it’s the time for us to change all of that. When one of us succeeds, we all get a little bit more powerful.”

Other individuals were also inducted into the organization’s CMO Hall of Fame, and various community organizers and tastemakers gave testimonials on We Are All Human’s impact in their lives. The late labor leader Dolores Huerta was also honored in a moving tribute, and Chavarria also mentioned the feminist activist in his speech. “She carried such strength and humanity and grace, and we all learned from her,” the designer said. “In this time when we see our brothers and sisters and our brown friends and family being treated like animals and abducted and sent away and put in camps and all of that, it’s just so important for us to stand tall in who we are right now.”

Cirque du Soleil took the stage to perform, and guests were given shots of Sotol Romo in champagne flutes for a toast. Co-chairs Gabriel de Alba, founder and managing partner of GDA Luma Capital Management; Karla Martínez de Salas, chief content officer of AVANCE; Bing Chen, CEO and co-founder of Gold House; and Marissa Solis, SVP of global brand and consumer marketing of the NFL, also attended the event. We Are All Human also surpassed its fundraising goals, with two individuals spending $32,000 on a Super Bowl package during the live auction.

“The We Are All Human Foundation is equipped to turn this momentum into results, through data and insights, to guide decisions and to inspire others,” Romo Edelman told the crowd. “Our co-chairs and honorees are the pure embodiment of the Latino brand that we want the world to see.”

Samuel is the Content Strategy Manager at Hearst. Prior to this role, he was an Associate Editor and the Assistant to ELLE’s Editor-in-Chief, Nina Garcia. Raised in Des Moines, Iowa, Samuel attended Northwestern University and currently resides in New York City. He is probably humming a tune at his desk right now.

#6832. Vogue Editors Predict the Hottest Coats of the Coldest Season

While winter technically starts on December 21, we’re calling it now: the season has officially begun. We feel confident in this pronouncement because, here in New York, all around us, jackets are finally manifesting. On sidewalks, in subway cars, hanging on crammed racks at the entrance of restaurants, on the backs of stylish passersby—everywhere we look, there are trenches, puffers, shearlings, bikers, blousons, sleek gorpy jackets, and so many more. Every shape, color, fabric, and mood a person can imagine is represented by a fetching piece of outerwear. Naturally, of course, we have some thoughts on what will be crowned the coat of the season. With that in mind, we asked Vogue editors around the office to take a stab at what they think the hottest coat of the winter 2026-27 season will be. Here are a few very educated guesses.

“In the spirit of the forthcoming Met Gala, a coat that is more than ordinary. Caroline Bille Brahe is brilliant at taking a classic, like a winter tweed or a classic duffel and working her magic on it by adding strong shoulders and a yoke, or storybook decorations.” —Laird Borrelli-Persson, senior archive editor

Caro Editions Caro wool coat in brown and green check, $1,505Caro Editions Thea wool coat in navy, $1,880

“Conner Ives certainly did not invent the fur-trimmed chinoiserie coat, but his spring 2027 runway—plus its cadre of celebrity fans—sent everyone from the ladies who lunch to the louche downtown set clamoring for opulent outerwear. Don’t have six grand for one of Ives’ coats? There are already plenty of mass market interpretations in the works—plus a host of enterprising TikTokers sharing how to make your own.” —Hannah Jackson, senior fashion writer

Connor Ives Reconstituted Vintage Fur and Silk Robe Coat in Black, £6,500

“Coat necklines have been going higher and higher every season, so this winter, I predict the full-on funnel neck coat will be huge. I love how structured-yet-sleek the silhouette is. Phoebe Philo has luxe trench or leather versions, but there are also affordable ones too, like this gray Mango wool style. And the best part? They cover your neck entirely—meaning, one less layer you have to pile on in the winter months.” — Christian Allaire, senior fashion and style writer

Phoebe Philo Cropped Trench, $2,600Phoebe Philo Swaithe Jacket $8,500Mango 100% Wool Funnel-Neck Coat, $209.99

“As a Prada devotee, I saw this jacket go down the runway back in January and was immediately obsessed—it was pure Prada: subversive, distinctive, slightly off-putting and totally amazing. Its classic khaki cotton edges are fraying and crumbling away, revealing hints of traditional houndstooth at the hems and seams (and, in a particularly brilliant move, replacing the triangular logo at the yoke). But it’s also the most classic of shapes, easy to wear with practically anything. An amazing coat, 10/10. The only drawback (for me, at least) is that five-figure price tag. At least it’s a nice round number …?” —Max Berlinger, senior fashion news editor

“I’ve been wanting a lightweight plaid mackintosh for a minute now. I want something really long and with a classic approach to the pattern, and I found this on Massimo Dutti last week. I’ve been seeing these out on the streets a bit, it’s just such an easy way to add a little energy to an outfit, especially if you tend to wear darker colors (like me).” —Max Berlinger, senior fashion news editor

Massimo Dutti Long Plaid Trench Coat, $490

“There is no more dominant jacket style than the mockneck bomber at this very moment—and you can thank Phoebe Philo for that. Still, despite her undeniable influence, whether the jacket is suede, leather, or technical, the most important part is the uber-studied, ultimately effortless Olsen tuck.” - Alexandra Hildreth, fashion news writer

Phoebe Philo Rib Neck Black Leather Jacket, $8,000 Nour Hammour Quince Soft Suede Jacket in Mocha, $1,885Cos Leather Mock Neck Leather Bomber Jacket, $549

“Decadent, novelty overcoats are causing a frenzy. They might not be the most practical (or keep you very warm, for that matter), but they sure will make the outfit. They range from Colleen Allen’s velvet opera coats to Kallmeyer and Chan Luu’s jacquard dusters. Special shoutout to the Conner Ives vintage fur-trimmed satin coats that have been breaking the internet. Even Nour Hammour’s shearling and faux fur-trimmed coats are making outerwear a little more extra this winter. Here’s to making the everyday more extraordinary or, simply put, making your coat the look.” —Madeline Fass, fashion director, Vogue Shopping

Nour Hammour Sophie 90s Leather Jacket, $2,120Kallmeyer Henri Floral Metallic-Jacquard Coat, $2,120Colleen Allen High Collar Velvet Coat, $3,000

“The Vogue girls cleared house and won at Arma’s mahjong night a few weeks ago, which means that a few of us will be wearing our field jackets for the next few months. But while we may have won our jackets, the brand has been on fire since their presentations in New York and Paris last season. In fact, eagle-eyed Vogue.com readers may have even clocked their leopard coat, which has been photographed by Phil Oh multiple times in each Fashion Week city. But I like how the field jacket feels oversized and casual enough to wear with a plain sweater or even with a dressier jacket.” —Irene Kim, editorial production manager

“Now that we’ve dredged all that we can from grandma’s attic, I think the next place to pull from is another house … the house of god. Stay with me, here: I think with Tom Ford’s Cry to Heaven on its way, and Pope Leo’s cultural dominance, we’ll see some monastic silhouettes beginning to emerge. Think the buttoned and buckled capes of Lanvin and Ann Demeulemeester, Nanushka's cheek-grazing collars, and the ecclesiastical severity of Mame Kurogouchi or Max Mara’s fall 2026 collections. It doesn’t have to mean austere—I love the drama of a mass! More like medieval monk meets modern minimalist, let’s say. I particularly love this La Veste Veste red and black cape that feels made for delivering the best homily of your life.”

“I’ve also come to embrace the bitchy little blazer—The Gilded Age’s Louisa Jacobson being a big reference here. She loves some sexy Tom Ford suiting with a sharp-as-hell lapel. New kids on the block, Catalogue NYC are making slim, gently cinched versions while Antwerp’s La Collection offers up decadent texture with their Margaret blazer. Brenda from accounts, this is not.”

“Despite their more tempered winters, Spanish women really know how to do good outerwear. And La Veste (which has been hosting a pop-up in New York) transitioned from a summer of sparkly short-shorts and circus tent-striped sets into sumptuous, candy-colored wool blazers and car coats. Violet, chartreuse, and funky combo stripes abound! Pro tip: La Veste co-founder Blanca Miro has collaborated with IYKYK Italian vintage dealer La Soffitta di Lulù on a stunning mini collection of fur-lined robes in sunshine yellow, sky blue, and unexpected prints.” —Anna Cafolla, news editor

“I think we’ll see something rich, opulent, decadent emerge this season, a response to the sleek, streamlined and, indeed, minimal vibes that have had a stronghold on winter fashion for a few years (see above: Connor Ives’s fur and silk robe coat). I can think of no better example than this plushy Dries Van Noten coat in an acid tone with a sumptuous surface and a regal collar. In fact, if I were a betting man, I’d say this exact model may just be THE coat of the season.” —Max Berlinger, senior fashion news editor

#6830. How a GQ Editor Is Wearing Abercrombie & Fitch YPB This Fall

Abercrombie & Fitch’s resurgence has been well documented, and the brand shows no signs of slowing down. Alongside its familiar mix of timeless staples, contemporary silhouettes, and archival-inspired pieces, Abercrombie has introduced YPB, or Your Personal Best: a dedicated line of performance apparel designed to bring the same considered approach to the gym as it does to the rest of your wardrobe.

Comprising everything from tees and tanks to shorts and jackets, YPB reflects Abercrombie’s ability to evolve while staying true to its heritage. The collection makes a convincing case for performance wear that goes beyond the usual sea of uninspired basics and head-to-toe Lycra. It’s also versatile enough to seamlessly move from a strenuous workout to the everyday wardrobe rotation. To put the collection through its paces, we’ve styled three looks that show just how far YPB can go.

I am a chronic overheater so my gym outfits always reveal a bit of skin. (It’s also a vanity thing so I can see my muscles at work when I’m getting after it.) This vintage-inspired muscle tank looks like some of the actual vintage tees that I’ve taken a pair of scissors to without a stranger’s set-in stains. I have a lot of hair that gets in my way so headwear is a must when working out. A bandana is a nice throwback to the classic bodybuilder era and unlike a hat, it does a better job at soaking up the sweat so it’s not dripping down my face.

The standout of this outfit is the shorts. Compression lined, they’re about as long as I’d go for shorts clocking in with a five-inch inseam. They have a discreet pocket in the liner to store my phone, and they're tight enough so my device doesn’t go flying out when I’m doing high knees. Plus, they’re stretchy enough for putting ass to grass on a squat without risking a NSFW tear between the cheeks.

I’ve come to learn that recovery days are not only a blessing but a necessity. But they don’t necessarily mean you have to waste away on the couch all day. My active recovery days involve a lot of walking, and that means my workout shorts make an appearance once again. I can’t deny their comfort factor, and it’s hard to beat a sweater-and-shorts combo, an outfit beloved by my favorite A-listers.

The sweater was a quarter-zip with an elastic waistband for a more streamlined, tailored fit. And if I’m walking a little too briskly, the top easily comes off to reveal a staple graphic tee in my wardrobe.

Finally, I put on some pants! I don’t make it a habit to wear sweatpants out casually, but sometimes the weather calls for it. Hike ‘em up a bit and show off some crisp white socks, a style swerve I saw once and couldn’t help but copy.

The staple of this outfit is the heavyweight jacket. Its water-resistant lining keeps me dry when the meteorologists get the forecast wrong, and it’s lined to keep me warm as the days get shorter and the nights get longer. The two-way zipper also allows for some extra mobility, and it won’t bunch up when I sit down like so many other parkas.

#6829. Inside Citymeals on Wheels’ 39th Annual Power Lunch at The Plaza

In New York City, a lunch reservation at The Plaza is always a good idea. But on Thursday afternoon, there was a particularly good reason to be there. Around 400 guests from the fashion, business, entertainment, and philanthropy worlds arrived at the storied hotel for Citymeals on Wheels’ 39th annual Power Lunch, raising more than $1.3 million to help feed older New Yorkers.

This year’s honorees included New York City police commissioner Jessica Tisch, Imaginary Ventures co-founder Dame Natalie Massenet, and Today co-host Al Roker, each honored for their longtime support of Citymeals. Deborah Roberts, a Citymeals board member and ABC News correspondent, served as emcee.

A number of familiar faces from the city’s social scene turned out, including Karlie Kloss, Lauren Santo Domingo, Tamara Mellon, and Derek Blasberg. Event chairs Blasberg, Dr. Samantha Boardman, Margo M. Nederlander, and Lizzie Tisch helped bring the afternoon together, alongside Citymeals board co-presidents Anne Cohen and Julie Daum.

Of course, the most important number of the afternoon wasn’t the guest count. The funds raised will provide approximately 130,000 meals to older residents across the five boroughs, where Citymeals currently serves 22,000 people.

For Citymeals CEO Beth Shapiro, the afternoon was a reminder of what a gathering like this can accomplish. “The generosity we saw in the room today is a powerful reminder of what’s possible when New Yorkers come together to care for one another,” she said in a statement.

Scroll below for a look at the familiar faces who gathered at The Plaza for this year’s Power Lunch.

Moriel is the editorial and social media assistant at ELLE.com, covering celebrity, culture, and fashion. She previously wrote for The Daily Front Row. When she's off work, you can find her with her nose in a book, taking a dance class, or online shopping.

#6828. Shop Our Favorite Celebrity Looks of the Week

Fall is here! If you’re wondering what to wear to embrace the drop in temperatures, we’re here to simplify matters with outfit ideas, courtesy of our favorite celebrities spotted on the streets. Consider this week’s edit your guide to everything from transitional fall looks to clever layering techniques, all infused with plenty of off-duty flair.

This week, celebrities embraced the seasonal chills, stepping out in their best fall outerwear—which for many meant a faux-fur jacket and jeans. Hailey Bieber wore Phoebe Philo’s sold-out shearling Dancer jacket with straight-leg Levi’s jeans and strappy mules for an event in New York, while Bella Hadid layered her faux Mango topper (also sold out!) over a sporty zip-up, bootcut denim, cap-toe heels, and Coach’s Chelsea bag while in Aspen. Julia Garner stepped out in a faux-fur-trimmed coat from The Andamane, pairing it with light-wash jeans, Loewe’s Amazona bag, and quilted ballerina flats. If there’s one cold-weather layer worth investing in this season, a faux fur jacket is certainly it.

Other outerwear inspiration came from Olivia Munn, who wore a minimalist black mac coat over a taupe turtleneck sweater and Ossou’s Flex jeans in an indigo wash—the perfect everyday outfit. Rihanna, also a Phoebephile, took a more playful approach to her black leather bomber and jeans formula, adding a dose of color with Dries Van Noten’s rainbow-striped sneakers and a coordinating oversized tote.

Keep reading to discover these ideas and more, bringing timeless classics to life with a few standout finds, all reworked by the stars and completely shoppable.

Hailey Bieber ushered in the season of statement outerwear with Phoebe Philo’s sold-out shearling Dancer jacket for an event in New York this week. She dressed up her favorite pair of Levi’s jeans with strappy mules, a sleek black clutch, and diamond studs. Consider this the perfect formula for date nights and holiday gatherings alike.

Looking for some easy everyday inspiration? Olivia Munn’s recent look is a good place to start. The actress wore a minimalist black mac coat over a taupe turtleneck sweater and Ossou’s Flex jeans in an indigo wash, finishing with black pointy pumps. We’d simply add a structured top-handle bag to complete this timeless pairing.

Jennifer Lawrence is leaning into all things lavish for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping press tour. Think embroidery, velvet, jacquard, feathers—nothing is off limits. Her styling trick? Balancing elaborate pieces with something simple, like a white V-neck T-shirt and jeans. Take a similar approach, adding strappy mules and her Completedworks earrings for a striking finish.

Bella Hadid is already in après-ski mode. The supermodel was spotted in Aspen, layering her sold-out, faux-fur Mango topper over a sporty navy zip-up and bootcut denim for a cool off-duty look, while Coach’s Chelsea bag and cap-toe heels added polished touches. Whether just off the slopes or city-bound, this one’s worth bookmarking.

Katie Holmes stepped out with boyfriend Jason Bard Yarmosky for Old Navy’s festive fête in New York in the ideal party-season pairing. Recreate the look with an oversized gray sweater, sequin-fringe skirt, and contrasting leopard-print kitten heels. The mix of cozy knits, playful sparkle, and unexpected pattern keeps the outfit feeling interesting without looking overly put together.

Julia Garner stepped out in a faux-fur-trimmed coat by The Andamane (another sold-out style), but you can recreate the look with a similar wrap silhouette. Ground the statement topper with light-wash jeans, Loewe’s Amazona bag, and black ballet flats for an off-duty take, then finish with a pair of oversized sunglasses from Side Eye for an extra dose of downtown cool.

Sarah Pidgeon demonstrated the art of set dressing at Chanel’s Watches and Fine Jewelry dinner in a matching gray shirt-and-trouser combination. She wore the shirt open over a white T-shirt, breaking up the monochromatic look, and accessorized with classic cap-toe pumps and a tiger’s eye beaded necklace. It’s the cool-girl take on a tailored two-piece combo.

Rihanna, another Phoebephile, took a more playful approach to her black leather bomber by Ms. Philo. Paired with baggy jeans, the casual look received playful contrast from Dries Van Noten’s rainbow-striped sneakers and a coordinating oversized tote, proving the most laid-back uniform can feel fresh with a little color therapy.

Minimalists can still have a little fun with evening dressing, even if it comes down to the subtlest details. Ella Rubin wore a black Chanel jacket accented with candy-colored stone buttons, pairing it with slouchy slim jeans and satin slingbacks for a dinner celebrating the house. It’s the kind of low-key glamour that works well beyond office hours.

Want more? Shop the best celeb outfits from last week, below.

Kendall Jenner was spotted wearing The Row’s riff on the barn jacket while strolling through the West Village with boyfriend Jacob Elordi. The supermodel styled the military green chore coat with Éterne’s bootcut denim, brown leather boots, and a roomy tote bag for a minimalist take on casual weekendwear. A leopard-print scarf provided a playful contrast to her otherwise understated look.

For a shopping trip at The Grove in Los Angeles, Rihanna chose a simple khaki trench coat as her fall outerwear piece du jour, layering it over a pale pink button-down shirt and relaxed brown jeans. Miu Miu x New Balance suede sneakers added a sporty finish, while Saint Laurent’s translucent pink sunglasses and Louis Vuitton’s Speedy bag elevated the everyday staples with designer flair.

Zoë Kravitz’s gold streak continues. She first embraced the trend at the CFDA Awards in a Saint Laurent dress, doubling down on gilded glamour this week while attending the New York premiere of How to Rob a Bank in a coordinated set from Anthony Vaccarello’s final collection for the French house. Re-create the idea with a shrunken metallic jacket and brocade flare trousers, finished with strappy heels, a sleek clutch, and diamond drop earrings. Jennifer Lawrence continues to stand by the velvet flats trend. The actress was spotted in a ruby-red Friulane style from The Row, styled with a black blazer and wide-leg trousers. The textural interplay continued with a croc-embossed top-handle bag (another major accessory trend this season!) and a devoré velvet scarf, proving that the right accessories can really transform even the simplest outfit.

The actress wore a chocolate-brown Louis Vuitton jacket as a top, featuring a nipped-in waist and ornamental closures. Its subtle curved silhouette paired perfectly with straight-leg blue jeans and pointy pumps. Finish with a top-handle bag, oval sunnies, and a simple belt for an effortlessly polished look that transitions from day to night with ease.

Another take on the peplum trend, Louisa Jacobson chose a full look from Ashlyn’s spring 2027 show for a Tiffany & Co. event in New York. Until the runway look is shoppable, capture the idea with a curved cardigan from the brand and a slinky green tube skirt. Meghann Fahy knows that when all else fails, an all-black ensemble never disappoints. Pointy pumps and shield sunglasses gave the monochromatic look a Matrix-inspired style point of view with a bit of downtown attitude.

Paloma Elsesser demonstrated how to make a single-tone ensemble feel more interesting, with texture and unexpected silhouettes serving as the secret sauce. Rosie Huntington-Whiteley stepped out in Phoebe Philo’s burgundy leather bomber jacket, pairing it with a plain white T-shirt, gray pleated trousers, and pointed black ankle boots from Christen. Chloë Sevigny broke out her Fair Isle knitwear early, wearing a patterned sweater over a white polo shirt and denim midi skirt while out and about in New York. While promoting the new season of All’s Fair, Naomi Watts stepped out in a double-breasted pinstripe blazer. When it came to accessories, however, she went all in, adding a floral brooch, an oversized-buckle belt, and a printed silk scarf. Here, more is more.

Rihanna made a case for easy monochrome dressing, wearing Phoebe Philo’s brown crewneck sweater with khaki trousers for a night out in Los Angeles. The trick is mixing complementary shades within the same color family. Minimalist pumps, oversized sunglasses, and understated jewelry—including diamond hoops and a metal choker necklace—take the look effortlessly from day to night.

What’s more luxe than a sweeping velvet house coat? Katie Holmes wore a burgundy leather bomber jacket and striped sweater from Banana Republic’s recent collaboration with Zankov on a sunny day in New York. Hailey Bieber proves the easiest way to liven up wardrobe staples is with a bright outerwear piece. She added a cobalt pop to her black T-shirt and kick-flare trouser combination with a vibrant Mac coat, sticking to her go-to accessories: The Row’s Penelope mules and a burgundy flap shoulder bag. The result is an easy day-to-night formula for transitional weather.

Louisa Jacobson was spotted making the rounds on The Gilded Age press tour in a full look by Mel Usine. The ensemble comes straight from the brand’s spring 2027 collection and is available for pre-order. The actress made it her own with heeled peep-toe mules and sunglasses from Thistles (she’s a face of the brand). We’d simply add a standout mini bag to complete the look.

The groutfit is back. Meghann Fahy made a case for the simplicity of it all—wearing a matching Almina Concept shirt and trousers while promoting her new project, The Good Daughter. She kept things streamlined, accessorizing solely with glossy patent leather high-vamp pumps. Round out the look with a minimalist black bag, sleek sunglasses, and sculptural silver earrings.

Here, the actress layered it over her signature go-tos: an all-black crewneck sweater with All Three’s flowy wide-leg pants. Burgundy ballet flats, red sunglasses, and an easy nylon tote bag completed the sporty-meets-minimalist aesthetic—in short, the perfect transitional fall look.

Although Jennifer Lawrence often gravitates towards elevated basics, she still likes to add a bit of quirk into the mix. For a walk in New York, she wore an oversized navy crewneck sweater with a black T-shirt, styling them with distressed straight-leg jeans in a light wash and brown suede mules. A bold lime-green handbag added a vibrant, unexpected pop to the otherwise understated outfit.

While in Rome, Julianne Moore went for Italian simplicity while promoting her new film, The Debut. Recreate her full Bottega Veneta look with a black ink-hued cardigan layered over a white long-sleeve T-shirt, adding the house’s statement skirt and black kitten-heeled mules for a fashion-forward finish. Accessorize with a clean clutch and silver jewelry for an effortless desk-to-dinner approach.

Dakota Johnson was spotted in Los Angeles continuing her new boho streak, this time in a vintage Simon & Garfunkel T-shirt and baggy brown corduroy pants. She kept it modern in the accessories department with Valentino’s patchwork Panthea bag, black ballet flats, and diamond drop earrings. Just add a leather jacket on chillier days for that extra rock-and-roll twist.

For a walk in London, Sienna Miller took a transitional approach to fall dressing, pairing a relaxed navy sweater with tailored black Bermuda shorts. Knee-high leather boots and Bottega Veneta’s Cabat bag lent a dose of designer flair, while black aviator-inspired frames added a cool, off-duty edge. This one works just as well for weekend wanderings as it does for a casual office setting.

For an outing in New York, Karlie Kloss wore a cream pintucked blouse with a gray mini skirt, draping a cozy cashmere shawl over the shoulders to ward off unexpected chills. Black ballet flats, a structured everyday bag, and oval sunnies pulled the look together with signature flair. Consider this an easy office look to keep in rotation, especially on those in-between-season days.

#6827. White House warns Democrats against aggressive oversight

Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., is expected to lead the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call file photo)

The Trump administration signaled it would respond aggressively to a Democratic-led Congress with a letter this week threatening to prosecute lawmakers for oversight efforts.

The letter from White House Counsel Will Scharf sent Monday to House Oversight and Government Reform ranking member Robert Garcia, D-Calif., argued that members of Congress have limited authority to conduct oversight of a presidential administration and that some of the threats to issue subpoenas “may cross the line into blatant criminality.”

The letter, obtained from a White House official, marks the latest escalation from the Trump administration ahead of Democrats taking control of both chambers of Congress next year. It also dovetails with years of Trump’s threats to prosecute his critics.

“We are monitoring the abusive and capricious threats that are now proliferating from Democrat legislators who seek to abuse the legislative process to intimidate and to interfere with the lawful functioning of government,” the letter says.

Garcia, the likely committee chair next Congress, pushed back on the threat in a statement Wednesday, accusing the administration of having “something to hide” and that Congress has wide authority to investigate the executive branch.

“The American people voted overwhelmingly for us to pass laws to root out corruption and abuse," Garcia said. "The Trump Administration continues to weaponize the government with threats of unconstitutional attacks on Congress. We are a co-equal branch of government and will not be deterred by baseless threats from a weaponized DOJ or from the President’s lawyers.”

The letter came after Attorney General Todd Blanche previously refused to rule out criminal charges against members of Congress in response to investigations.

"It depends on what the crime is and what they have done,” Blanche told CNN over the weekend.

Last week, President Donald Trump himself said that threats of investigations and impeachment were “extortion at the highest level” and called for the Justice Department to “look into this criminal act, immediately!”

He also singled out Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., calling for her to be imprisoned. The administration previously unsuccessfully attempted to indict Slotkin and other Democrats over a video she published calling for soldiers to disobey illegal orders.

And Trump last year publicly called for longtime critic Sen. Adam B. Schiff, D-Calif., to face unspecified charges in a post on Truth Social addressed to then-Attorney General Pam Bondi that also called for the prosecution of former FBI Director James Comey and New York Attorney General Letitia James. Both have faced criminal charges, pleaded not guilty and fought them in court as political attacks.

Garcia and other Democrats have signaled they intend to pursue oversight aggressively in the new Congress. After Democrats won the House majority last week, Garcia put out an all-caps statement urging administration officials to “LAWYER UP” ahead of the new year.

Garcia, as well as other likely incoming chairs such as House Judiciary ranking member Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md.; Homeland Security ranking member Rep. Bennie Thompson, D-Miss.; and Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., have hinted at broad inquiries ranging from the handling of files related to deceased sex offender Jeffrey Epstein to immigration enforcement and more.

Raskin told reporters last week that he thought Democratic oversight efforts could dovetail with the party’s broader effort to address affordability issues, including by addressing the Iran war, allegations of corruption within the Trump administration and more.

“We're going to get all the information that we need in order to restore the rule of law in American constitutional democracy,” Raskin said.

The letter also echoes a previous fight the administration pitched with the House in the first Trump administration, where officials resisted in court allowing former White House Counsel Don McGahn to testify to the House Judiciary Committee for years.

#6825. Safe Word: The Best Jewelry Launches of November 2026

Safe Word is a series highlighting the latest trends in the jewelry market, keeping you up to date on all things that sparkle and shine.

November’s jewelry launches are looking both backward and forward, with designers revisiting their roots, reworking archival ideas, and stepping into entirely new territory. First up, Quentin Jones is taking her surrealist art off the wall and onto the body with “Nocturne,” her first jewelry collection; Pomellato reaches back to 1997 to revive “Moneta Orientale” as a colorful modern talisman; David Yurman celebrates the magic of a New York holiday with Michael B. Jordan, Yerin Ha, and Inde Navarrette; Vhernier revisits its iconic “Trottola” design with new proportions and contrasting materials; Di Volpe reinterprets the classic tennis bracelet with customizable gemstones in “DiSegno”; Brent Neale transforms the classic bow into sculptural fine jewelry with “Wrap It Up”; and Kendra Scott launches the new “Kendra Scott Collection,” reimagining her signature Spike motif as a personal talisman. From archival revivals and meaningful motifs to innovative designs and new creative directions, November’s launches prove that sometimes the best way forward starts with looking back. For the rest of the month, we’ve got you covered on all the jewelry-related happenings worth knowing about.

Quentin Jones is taking her art off the wall and onto the body with “Nocturne,” the first jewelry collection from House of Quentin Jones. Following the multidisciplinary artist’s debut of surrealist ceramics and tapestries last year, the new collection transforms recurring gestures and symbols from her work into sculptural collars, cuffs, armbands, pendants, chains, and earrings. Eyes, hands, stars, moons, tears, and knots take shape in silver and gold vermeil alongside freshwater pearls, onyx, opals, jade, glass, and silk tassels, giving the pieces a dreamlike, talismanic quality. Beginning as drawings and hand collages in Jones’s Brooklyn studio, each design carries her surrealist visual language into wearable form, further blurring the line between art, design, and fashion.

Piotrek Panszczyk Makes His Debut at Ippolita

Ippolita is entering a new chapter under creative director Piotrek Panszczyk, who makes his debut at the house with “Ancient Bohemia,” a collection inspired by its archives and the organic forms of nature. Taking a sculptural approach to jewelry, Panszczyk reimagines familiar signatures with an emphasis on texture, craftsmanship, and unconventional layering. The house’s iconic Wavy Disk becomes the Wavy Coin, featuring Hippolyta, Queen of the Amazons and the brand’s namesake, as a symbol of feminine strength. Elsewhere, hand-sculpted Stardust pavé is set entirely with diamonds, pearls make their first appearance, and lightweight, hand-hammered silver Roma links offer multiple ways to wear, from necklaces to belts. Lapis lazuli, mother-of-pearl, and quartz introduce color through Ippolita’s signature layered doublets and triplets, mixed rather than matched for an eclectic finish. The result is a fresh interpretation of the house’s heritage that feels both ancient and distinctly modern.

Jade Trau and Luis Morais Combine Gemstones and Diamonds

Jade Trau and Luis Morais are joining forces for a limited-edition collection that brings together their different approaches to fine jewelry. Comprised of 16 one-of-a-kind pieces, including 12 bracelets and four necklaces, the collaboration pairs Morais’s colorful gemstone beads with Trau’s signature 18-karat gold and diamond elements. The designs feature a vibrant mix of stones, from chrysoprase and amazonite to lapis lazuli, turquoise, carnelian, and tiger’s-eye, accented by recognizable Jade Trau details like the Frankie rondelle, Sophisticate station, and Georgie diamond lock. Designed with everyday wear in mind, the bracelets lend themselves to layering, while the necklaces incorporate Trau’s diamond-set closures. The result is a playful meeting of color and craftsmanship that brings a fresh perspective to both designers’ signatures.

Lagos Looks to the Stars With Its Latest Collection

Lagos references the night sky in its latest fine jewelry collection, taking inspiration from the North Star and its centuries-old symbolism of guidance and possibility. Designed to celebrate milestones, new beginnings, and meaningful connections, the “North Star” collection features sculptural star motifs crafted in 18-karat gold and illuminated by natural diamonds. Cascading silhouettes and light-catching details bring a sense of movement to the celestial designs, balancing statement-making shapes with delicate craftsmanship. Both symbolic and sophisticated, the assortment offers a modern interpretation of a timeless emblem, making each piece a reminder of the people and moments that guide us.

Kendra Scott Launches an Eponymous Collection

Kendra Scott is offering a more personal look into her design world with the launch of the “Kendra Scott Collection,” a new line spanning fashion and fine jewelry. Its first edition, “The Spike,” revisits a silhouette the designer has worn throughout her career as a personal symbol of strength, confidence, and conviction. Inspired by nature and the radiance of the night sky, the collection translates the pointed motif into sculptural necklaces, earrings, bracelets, and charms, balancing bold proportions with intricate craftsmanship. Fashion jewelry incorporates tiger’s eye, malachite, and turquoise, while fine jewelry introduces lab-grown diamonds, pavé detailing, labradorite, and lapis. From statement-making links to delicate diamond charms, the collection offers a new interpretation of Scott’s longtime signature, inviting wearers to make the symbol their own.

Alison Lou’s ‘New Wave’ Collection Experiments With New Materials

Alison Lou is entering a new chapter with “New Wave,” a fine jewelry collection that introduces unexpected materials and a fresh approach to the designer’s signature playful aesthetic. Exploring the relationship between movement and form, the collection pairs lightweight titanium and ceramic with lab-grown diamonds, creating fluid, sculptural silhouettes that curve and catch the light. Available in Fig and Denim Blue colorways, the designs include wavy rings, diamond-accented signets, delicate thread necklaces, and statement drop earrings. With its unconventional materials and easy-to-wear designs, “New Wave” brings a new sense of movement to Alison Lou’s everyday jewelry.

Jenny Bird and Emese Gormley Partner on the Anyu Ring

Jenny Bird is expanding her JB FINE collection with a new collaboration featuring lifestyle creator and Lipstick on the Rim podcast host Emese Gormley. Named in honor of Gormley’s mother, the Anyu Ring offers a personal take on the classic signet, featuring three lab-grown baguette diamonds set in 14-karat yellow or white gold. The understated design combines the timeless appeal of a signet ring with a sentimental tribute to family, bringing a new perspective to Bird’s growing fine jewelry offering. Available exclusively on Jenny Bird’s website, the collaboration makes a case for jewelry that feels as meaningful as it looks.

Pomellato Revives Its 1997 Moneta Orientale Pendant as a Colorful Talisman

Pomellato is looking to its archives for its latest good-luck charm. For the newest chapter of “Memorie d’Archivio,” the maison revives Moneta Orientale, a 1997 pendant inspired by the ancient symbolism of a circle surrounding a square, representing the harmony between heaven and earth. Made in 33 stone-and-pavé combinations, the design pairs colorful hard stones including black jade, amazonite, sodalite, rhodochrosite, and labradorite with Pomellato’s signature irregular pavé of diamonds, sapphires, rubies, and more. Offered in two proportions, each pendant transforms the archival motif into a modern talisman for prosperity and protection.

Bibi van der Velden Makes Her High Jewelry Debut With ‘Eclipse’

Bibi van der Velden is entering a new era with “Eclipse,” the designer’s first high jewelry collection and most refined exploration of diamonds to date. Inspired by the fleeting moment when light gives way to darkness, the collection includes two six-piece suites: one in white diamonds and another defined by an ombré of diamonds into gray spinels deepening into black. Van der Velden’s signature alligator motif is abstracted into fluid, sculptural silhouettes, with scales engraved into the white gold on the reverse of each piece. “With Eclipse, I wanted to take those familiar elements and transform them into something more abstract and sculptural,” she says. “It’s a collection about transformation, which has always been at the heart of my work.”

Aflalo and Leandra Medine Cohen Turn Everyday Indulgences Into Fine Jewelry

Aflalo is finding the humor in our obsession with wellness with “The Vanities,” a new two-piece fine jewelry capsule designed exclusively by Leandra Medine Cohen. Playing with the contradiction between longevity and life’s little indulgences, the collection transforms two unlikely everyday accessories into precious objects. The Memento Mori is a 14-karat yellow gold cigar band set with more than four carats of diamonds, designed to slip over an Oura Ring, while The Libertine is a sterling silver pendant case adorned with diamonds and a wild-haired woman outlined in gold, designed to hold nicotine pouches or other small essentials. Equal parts extravagant and irreverent, the collection makes a playful case for enjoying life’s pleasures without sacrificing personal style.

Julia Berolzheimer’s Hart Jewelry Collection Draws on Childhood Memories

Hart is teaming up with Julia Berolzheimer for a new jewelry collection that celebrates the art of the stack. Inspired by Berolzheimer’s childhood memories of her grandmother’s California ranch and her collection of Art Deco minaudières, the collaboration brings together whimsical charms, colorful gemstones, and meaningful talismans designed to be mixed, layered, and restyled. Botanical motifs take shape in Tree of Life coins, daisies, bees, and fruit-inspired charms, while carnelian, turquoise, and pink opal add playful pops of color. One standout is the Perfume Vesta Case, a modern interpretation of a Victorian-era accessory that can hold a sample-sized fragrance and hang alongside other charms. With interchangeable chains, cords, and pendants, the collection makes a case for jewelry that feels just as personal as the memories behind it.

David Yurman Captures the Magic of a New York Holiday

David Yurman is celebrating the magic of the holidays in New York City with a new campaign featuring global brand ambassador Michael B. Jordan alongside actresses Yerin Ha and Inde Navarrette. Set against a snow-covered Washington Square Park, the campaign captures a series of quintessential New York moments, from Jordan and Ha facing off in a spirited card game to Navarrette hailing a cab in search of the perfect holiday gift. Throughout the campaign, the cast wears some of the house’s most recognizable designs, including 18-karat gold Cable bracelets and pieces from the “Starburst” and “Armory” collections. Directed by Bradford Young and photographed by Drew Vickers, the campaign brings together the spirit of the city, the joy of togetherness, and the timeless appeal of David Yurman’s jewelry.

Vhernier Reintroduces Its Iconic ‘Trottola’ Design With New Proportions

Vhernier is revisiting one of its most recognizable designs with a new interpretation of “Trottola,” the sculptural collection originally introduced in 2003. Inspired by the continuous motion of a spinning top, the latest designs play with proportions, contrasting materials, and asymmetrical shapes across rings, bracelets, necklaces, and earrings. Polished rose gold meets glossy black jet, with select pieces featuring diamond pavé for an added contrast of light and dark. The collection also focuses on versatility, from rings designed for stacking to convertible earclips that can be worn as studs or dangling earrings. With its fluid forms and unexpected material combinations, “Trottola” brings a fresh perspective to Vhernier’s signature sculptural approach to jewelry.

Di Volpe is rethinking the classic tennis bracelet with “DiSegno,” a new customizable fine jewelry system designed to change with its wearer. Using concealed, patent-pending connections, individual cultured diamonds and gemstones, called Elements, can be removed, rearranged, or added by hand, allowing wearers to transform bracelets into necklaces or earrings without compromising the seamless look of traditional tennis jewelry. The collection launches with 28 stone-and-cut combinations, including rubies, emeralds, sapphires, and diamonds, alongside a limited-edition collaboration with Lebanese artist Ali Cha’aban featuring five sculptural designs. With new cuts, colors, and artist collaborations planned for future releases, “DiSegno” makes the case for fine jewelry that’s never quite finished.

Brent Neale Riffs on the Bow in Fine Jewelry

Brent Neale is putting a bow on the holiday season with “Wrap It Up,” a new fine jewelry collection that transforms the familiar ribbon motif into sculptural works of art. Drawing inspiration from Old Hollywood glamour and the femininity of the 1960s, the designer plays with the contrast between rigid precious metals and the soft movement of fabric, crafting bows that twist, curl, and unfurl in 18-karat gold and platinum. Colored gemstones sit nestled within the ribbon-like forms, while pavé diamonds accentuate every curve and fold. Equal parts playful and precious, the collection brings a little gift-wrapped glamour to the jewelry box.

Grace Winfrey’s ‘Poppy Fortuna’ Collection Reimagines Good-Luck Charms

Grace Winfrey is bringing a little extra luck to the jewelry box with “Poppy Fortuna,” a new fine jewelry collection inspired by the natural beauty of the Italian landscape and symbols of good fortune. Scarlet poppies, sunflowers, bees, four-leaf clovers, horseshoes, and ladybugs come to life through vibrant gemstones and intricate pavé, creating miniature mosaics of color and texture. Highlights include a Lucky Bangle combining three good-luck charms, sculptural sunflower earrings with tiny ladybugs tucked into their petals, and layered charm necklaces designed to feel like modern keepsakes. Handcrafted in New York City, each piece transforms familiar symbols of prosperity, protection, and happiness into playful, colorful works of art.

Robinson Pelham Channels ’90s Glamour for Its Anniversary

Robinson Pelham is closing out its 30th anniversary celebrations with “Suite 96,” a new campaign and collection launch inspired by the glamour of late-’90s London. Set inside a private suite at St. James’s Hotel & Club in Mayfair, the campaign considers jewelry the ultimate room service, with diamonds arriving on trays, gold spilling out of wardrobes, and plenty of pieces to layer before a night out. At the center is “Studio 30,” a four-piece anniversary collection featuring diamond necklaces and statement earrings, including the sculptural Via and Hira necklaces, cascading diamond drops, and the bold Solstice Supreme. Alongside the anniversary designs, the house introduces new collections and additions to existing favorites, from chunky gold links and graphic heart rings to colorful enamel and gemstone combinations. Together, the launches celebrate three decades of Robinson Pelham’s bold, playful approach to fine jewelry.

Le Vian and Jared Revive Georgian-Era Romance

Le Vian is bringing a little old-world romance to Jared Jewelers with its new exclusive “Georgian Chocolate & Nude Diamonds” collection. Inspired by the candlelit jewels of the Georgian era, when jewelry was designed to capture and reflect the warmth of natural light, the collection rethinks historic buttercup settings in polished Honey Gold, with eight rounded prongs framing each natural diamond. The designs pair Le Vian’s signature Chocolate and Nude Diamonds with warm gold detailing across solitaire rings, anniversary bands, tennis bracelets, necklaces, and earrings. Select styles introduce colorful gemstones including Chocolate Quartz, Green Apple Peridot, and Grape Amethyst, giving the vintage-inspired silhouettes a contemporary update. With its sculptural settings and warm-toned stones, the collection brings the romance of antique jewelry into the present.

Wempe’s ‘Au:thentic’ Celebrates the Art of Goldsmithing

Wempe’s new gender-inclusive fine jewelry collection, “Au:thentic,” puts craftsmanship front and center, finding inspiration in the foundational skills taught to aspiring goldsmiths. The collection takes its shape from the jump ring, one of the first techniques Patrick Sieroslawski learned as an apprentice more than 22 years ago, translating its form to necklaces, bracelets, rings, earrings, and pendants. Handcrafted at Wempe’s atelier in Germany, the pieces come in 18-karat yellow, white, and rose gold, with select styles set with diamonds. “Au:thentic” also marks the beginning of a multiyear rollout, with three additional chapters set to expand on its design language through twists, wraps, and interlocking links.

#6824. Gordon Ramsay’s Routine for a Six-Pack at 60 Includes Daily Crunches and Red-Light Therapy

Gordon Ramsay has earned 17 Michelin stars throughout his career and still oversees nearly 100 restaurants. He also fronts prime-time TV franchises on both sides of the Atlantic and holds a couple of casual Guinness World Records (call him if you need to fillet a 10-pound fish in 1 minute five seconds).

This is a man who’s never met a goalpost he didn’t want to surpass. So it wasn’t entirely surprising when he posted a bare-chested shot of his six-pack to the grid earlier this month. What generated headlines was the occasion: his 60th birthday. “Gordon Ramsay thirst trap was not on my bingo card,” reads one comment. “My wife is on this app sir,” reads another.

At home in London, he shows me the Insights section on his Instagram account, which reveals the photo has gotten over 62 million impressions. “It’s very strange,” he says. “I’ve had a lot of ribbing from my eldest daughter, Megan. She’s a police officer. She was like, ‘Dad, how can you do that to me?’ All her senior sergeants and officers were laughing and telling her to tell me they’re going for a run. They’re in their early 40s. And then my Royal Marines Commando son just sent me a message with: ‘WTF dad, what are you doing?’”

Ramsay has been a pretty active guy for a while now, despite working in an industry typically associated with chaotic diets and zero time for exercise. He was a youth soccer player back in the day, before becoming a chef and then, in his 40s, going from weighing 252 pounds to competing in marathons and Ironmans.

All very impressive, but it’s even rarer to be this chiseled in your 60s (maintaining a low body fat percentage becomes harder as your testosterone and growth hormone production slows down). Read on to learn more about his preferred forms of cardio, his favorite pre-workout treat, and why he's established a daily cryotherapy routine. “I call it my freezer,” he says.

“15 minutes a day. It starts off with a quick two-minute stretch and 100 sit-ups every morning. Precore lifestyle is my ab cruncher thing—these things are fucking amazing, by the way. If I miss a day, then I have to punish it and do double the next day.”

“It’s not physically hard with big weights. These are 25 pounds. I’ll do a strength class once a week, 45 minutes. That’s it. Occasional push-ups and squats. No personal trainer.”

“What’s helped tremendously, with no impact on any of the joints, is a lot of swimming. So I have an injury in my patella, my right knee, currently. So I just increased the swimming because that’s the only sport that can use every muscle in your body with zero impact. But cardio is off the charts.”

“I have a Zwift bike, so I jump on that for 45 minutes. There’s no impact on that. I’ll do that Monday, Wednesday, Friday and gear up for 90 minutes on a Sunday. If I wasn’t injured, I’d be doing three 5K runs again, Monday, Wednesday, Friday, 20-minute runs. I’ve got my 5K back down to 21 minutes. The dream is under 20. I was running at 19 and a half back in July. A 5K run is easy to do in the morning before work, it’s done within half an hour. Once I do that, I can gear up for either a two-hour bike on a Sunday or a 90-minute run. I alternate. So, one Sunday’s run, one Sunday’s bike.”

“10 years ago, I ruptured my Achilles. I invested in an AlterG, a beautiful running machine that takes your weight, so you get all the cardio you want and less impact on the joint.”

“From the chef’s perspective, I call it my freezer. It’s the cryochamber. I do two sets of three minutes every morning. I try to go seven days a week in that thing, straight after [working out]. That is incredible. That’ll get up to like minus 160. For six minutes.”

“I’ve invested in a tiny little red-light therapy sauna outside in the garden, and it seats two of you, and so [I’ll do] half an hour of that, every other day. This doesn’t need to be done every day. Three times a week’s fine. So when I’m not running, the other day I’ll sit in that red-light therapy and spend 20 minutes, 30 minutes in there, which is brilliant.”

“The older you get, the more you have to stretch. I use a lot of bands. And so after sitting and stretching, I had those incredible bands where you lift your feet up and pull and stretch. 5 minutes is always a nice stretch before you [work out] and then 10 minutes stretch after that. I’ve never been to a yoga class in my life.”

“I’m big on oatmeal for breakfast, Monday to Friday. I indulge Saturday, Sunday. I will do [oatmeal with] blueberry compote, caramelized banana for my potassium, and then fresh blueberries on top with some—it sounds weird, but it’s delicious—hot honey.”

“I have my friends at Precision. I’ll do one of their gels before I start that 5K, a protein gel, 30 grams, and then that sees me through the whole 45-minute routine. Coffee is just a full-fat, flat white, extra hot. Extra hot means I can sip it slowly. I cut out a lot of dairy, a lot of butter, a lot of cream. And so that treat in the morning with a flat white is that sort of, ‘I’ve earned this shit.’”

“I don’t overstress on that because I stay fit. I monitor what I eat, but if anything, I’ll do smaller portions now. I’ll involve a lot of spinach, involve a lot of salmon, chicken, especially thighs. We’re just smart with less cream, less butter intake. And then when we travel, we just keep it light.”

“I have a red wine with dinner, Californian, something light, something delicious. In 20, 30 years running restaurants, I’ve never gone around the room holding a glass of wine, holding a glass of champagne, sitting down, drinking with customers. Again, discipline.”

“Just a couple of spoons of creatine, five mornings a week. A little scoop in my water.”

“One thing I’ve learned in my 50s and my 60s—everyone said the older you get, the less you sleep. I think it’s the other way around. I like to be in bed by 11, and I’m up at 6. My Oura ring for me has become my best mate, because it just gives me the proper day-by-day indication and then keeps you on track for sleep.”

“Sign up for something. Have a target because that gets you out of bed, with a bigger, incentivized plan. I need that target twice a year, every six months. And I’ve done that since my 40th birthday. Whether it’s half an Ironman, whether it’s a marathon, half a marathon, I’ve always got something to focus on.”

“No, no, no, no, no, no. Definitely not. No. I mean, no. My meditation is Kitchen fucking Nightmares. Dealing with some of those contributors on there and having to sit with them and talk with them. But no, not very good at sitting still.”

A version of this story originally appeared in British GQ.

#6822. Holiday Travel With Babies and Pets Just Got a Whole Lot Easier

Smart travel essentials for the whole family—four-legged members included.

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Seasonal travel is exciting, but getting everyone from point A to point B can be a production—especially when babies and pets are involved. Between navigating crowded airports, packing the car with what feels like half your house, and keeping your four-legged family members calm amid all the chaos, there’s a ton to think about. And while you can’t control flight delays, holiday traffic, or the timing of a much-needed diaper change, having the right travel gear can make a world of difference.

Enter Nuna and Tavo, two brands that bring thoughtful design, innovative safety features, and a beautiful aesthetic to (often hectic) family travel. Nuna’s premium baby gear helps take some of the stress out of everything from airport security to car-seat installations, while Tavo focuses the same level of attention on the safety and comfort of travel essentials designed specifically for pets. Think lightweight strollers that fold with one hand (because your other one is probably occupied), car seats that don’t require an online tutorial to install, and comfortable carriers that give your furry companions a safe spot of their own.

Whether you’re flying across the country to visit the grandparents, packing up for a holiday road trip, or exploring a new destination together, these six Nuna and Tavo essentials, available at Bloomingdale’s, can help make the journey a little more joyful for everyone involved.

Given crowded security lines, blowouts at the worst possible moment, and the sheer amount of stuff you have to tote, a lightweight stroller is a genuine lifesaver at the airport. At just 16.3 pounds, the Nuna VIAA cabn is designed to meet IATA cabin-size standards when folded with the armbar removed—though you’ll still want to double-check your airline’s requirements. One-handed steering makes navigating crowded terminals easier (especially when you’re juggling a much-needed iced coffee), while a roomy storage basket holds up to 22 pounds of diaper bags, coats, backup outfits, bottles, snacks, and approximately 47 things to keep your baby entertained. It even comes with a carrier bag for when it’s time to board.

This Nuna duo pairs the TRIV lx stroller, which folds with one hand and stands on its own, with the ultralight PIPA urbn infant car seat. And if you’ve ever broken a sweat or found yourself YouTubing car seat installation instructions for the 100th time, you’ll appreciate that this one clicks into place without a base, using its built-in pipaFIX rigid latch installation. Large rear wheels and all-wheel suspension pair with a spacious storage basket and handy tracking-device pocket to make the stroller ready for everyday outings.

The Nuna SWIV’s standout feature is button-activated 360-degree rotation on all four wheels, allowing it to move sideways and pivot through tight spaces without the struggle of squeezing through crowded airport lines and store aisles that clearly weren’t designed with strollers in mind. A one-handed recline with three positions, including a near-flat option, makes adjustments easy, and the stroller is travel-system-ready with any Nuna PIPA series infant car seat, allowing you to move baby from the car to the stroller.

The Tavo Crispin gives your pet a roomy, comfortable spot of their own, with mesh panels for ventilation and visibility so they can still keep eyes on their humans. It’s impact-tested and secures to your vehicle using lower anchors and a top tether, with a protective memory-foam guard for added peace of mind. And when the holiday travels are over, it collapses for easy storage without taking up precious space at home.

This Tavo travel system might be your new favorite on-the-road companion. The Maeve car seat attaches to the Roscoe Trek stroller frame, so you can go from the car to a festive outing without having to transfer your pup to a different carrier. All-terrain rear wheels and suspension make bumpy sidewalks easier to navigate, while one-touch brakes and a compact stroller fold come in handy when it’s time for a coffee stop or to load everything back into the car.

There’s a very particular type of heart-rate spike that comes with flying with a pet. The Tavo Dupree II has a chic carry-on design that’s also crash-tested, complete with built-in vehicle connectors and a protective memory-foam guard. You’ll still want to double-check your airline’s requirements before flying.

#6821. Maple Bourbon Chicken With Brussels Sprouts

If you, like most people, hear the term “bourbon chicken” and have no idea what it is, let me call it by its more common name: toothpick chicken. Yes, the suspiciously delicious chicken shelled out at mall food courts on toothpicks is most likely bourbon chicken. Popular at American Chinese or Cajun-style Chinese restaurants, the sticky-sweet chicken is the utter definition of delicious, luring weary shoppers into food courts to find refuge from the bubblegum pink sweatpants and ripped denim. This version takes cues from the classic but swaps in some autumnal ingredients to make it fit for the season. Charred brussels sprouts leaves and pecans add bulk, while maple syrup and apple cider vinegar give it that delightful tart-sweet flavor we know and love. Serve it over rice or noodles or all by its lonesome for a hearty dinner that will take you back to the '90s.

More chicken dinner winners here: Sheet-Pan Hot Honey Chicken and Peaches; Basil Chicken Stir-Fry; and Ginger-Garlic Chicken and Vegetable Stir-Fry.

Whisk one 1½" piece ginger, peeled, finely grated, 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, ⅓ cup bourbon, ⅓ cup pure maple syrup, ¼ cup apple cider vinegar, ¼ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes, 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, ¼ cup low-sodium soy sauce, and ½ cup water in a small bowl to combine. Set sauce aside.

Toss 1½ lb. skinless, boneless chicken breasts, halved crosswise, thinly sliced against the grain, remaining 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, and remaining 1 Tbsp. low-sodium soy sauce in a medium bowl until chicken is coated; set aside.

Heat 2 Tbsp. vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add 1 lb. brussels sprouts, halved through stems, leaves separated, and cook, stirring very occasionally, until just tender and blackened in spots, about 5 minutes. Transfer to another medium bowl.

Add more oil if pan looks dry and, working in batches if needed, arrange reserved chicken in a single layer and cook, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through, about 5 minutes. Transfer to bowl with brussels sprouts.

Add reserved sauce to same pan and bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring constantly, until thickened, about 1 minute. Remove pan from heat and return brussels sprouts and chicken to pan; top with 1 cup salted roasted pecans, coarsely chopped. Toss to coat in sauce. Serve chicken and brussels sprouts with steamed white rice if desired.

#6820. A Brief Guide to Grand Theft Auto VI’s Nike Sneaker Dupes

GTA 6 is finally out, which means we’ve got some in-game sneaker shopping to do. We’d already spotted Air Force 1 dupes in the trailers, but now that we can finally play the long-awaited masterpiece itself, we’re taking a closer look at what else is on the shelves. There are tons of different sneaker stores sprinkled throughout the game, and Eris—Rockstar’s fictional answer to Nike—has given us a lot to work through.

Even the name is a joke. Nike takes its name from the Greek goddess of victory, while Eris is the goddess of strife and discord—an appropriate choice for kicks you might buy with money from an armed robbery. The Swoosh has been replaced with a pointier, upside-down logo, and plenty of the sneakers baring the mark are instantly recognizable.

The Eris Rise Low is the obvious starting point. It’s the game’s AF1 equivalent, complete with the familiar paneled upper, perforated toebox, and a big, beefy sole underfoot. The Eris Strife 360, meanwhile, looks straight out of the Air Max 97 catalog. There’s the rippling upper, rounded toe, and long cushioning window underneath. Designed by Christian Tresser and released in 1997, the IRL sneaker’s silhouette took inspiration from water ripples, while the OG “Silver Bullet” finish drew on mountain bike components. Eris keeps enough of that shape for you to be able to spot it from across the shop.

Some versions get even more specific. There’s a white-and-orange Strife 360, for example, with oversized branding, contrasting lace loops, and printed side text that recalls Off-White’s own Air Max 97s. It isn’t a straight one-to-one recreation, but the reference feels pretty clear. An apparent take on the Off-White Air Force 1 Mid also appeared in the teasers. Someone at Rockstar is clearly a fan of Virgil Abloh’s work.

Then there’s the Eris Strife 90, with pairs that borrow heavily from the Air Max 90 “Infrared.” The bright red accents and sharp, aggressive lines are all there, with one colorway even adding black scribbles across the overlays.

Arguably the most iconic signature shoe of all time, the Air Jordan 1, gets a look in the game as well. The Eris Rook 1 High comes in leather and suede variations, with a tall ankle collar and laces running almost all the way up. There’s a black-and-white pair that swaps Jordan branding for an Eris basketball graphic on the tongue. You’ve probably got something quite similar in your closet at home.

The Eris Cross Trainers are, well, harder to pin down. Available in several colorways, they have a mesh base and leather overlays. One white-and-gray version gets bright green hits that nod to Nike’s signature “Volt” hue. The simpler construction puts it closer to an older Nike runner, somewhere around MD Runner 2 territory, than a direct Zoom Vomero 5 or V5 Rnr copy. And for those times that tying laces feels like too much work, there are the very appropriately named Eris Basic Slides. The broad branded strap and flat footbed are very Nike Benassi.

There are different versions to consider, too. “Origins” go all-white, while “Elite” options are matte and all-black. So if you‘ve found a silhouette you like, you can still spend another 10 minutes deciding which version works with your trousers. A problem we were hoping to leave outside the game.

It gives you an idea of just how much there is in GTA 6. The older games let you change your clothes, but here you’re choosing between different colorways, materials, and versions of individual shoes. And Eris is only one part of it: There are clothes and accessories that look like takes on Stüssy, Loewe, Chrome Hearts, and Louis Vuitton, too. You could spend a fair bit of time getting dressed before you get anything else done.

We’ve waited this long to play the game. A few more minutes in the sneaker shop before you really get going on missions won’t hurt.

#6818. Farrar, Straus and Giroux Celebrated Eight Decades of Literary Greats

Few literary presses can claim a Rolodex as studded with boldface names as Farrar, Straus and Giroux. This week, the publishing house, whose authors have been awarded dozens of National Book Awards, Pulitzer Prizes, and Nobel Prizes in Literature, toasted its 80th anniversary with a distinguished fête in Manhattan’s Chelsea neighborhood.

The guest list, which gathered prominent cultural and artistic personages, featured a mix of FSG’s coterie of best-selling writers from over the years. The night united early-career contemporary authors like Madeline Cash (Lost Lambs) and Raven Leilani (Luster) with established literary lions such as Jonathan Franzen, André Aciman, and Jeffrey Eugenides. The decorated crowd also included filmmaker John Waters, Emmy Award winner Rebecca Miller, actor and editor Tavi Gevinson, and booksellers James Daunt and Sarah McNally.

The evening was hosted by president and publisher Mitzi Angel, who became the first woman to lead the house when she stepped into her position in 2022. Before and during her tenure at FSG Angel worked with authors including Sheila Heti, Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie, Rachel Cusk, Garth Greenwell, and Sally Rooney. Though cognizant of the role of algorithms in the economy of taste, Angel expressed “great faith” in the current and future state of publishing and the literary arts. “I feel more certain than ever that good writing can arrive in our hands at any moment, from anywhere,” Angel told Vogue, surveying the mingling throng of writers she’d published. “I think all of us here in this room understand that it only takes one person to reframe reality altogether: one person, a writer.”

Guests were treated to a soaring performance of Philip Glass’s “Songs from Liquid Days” by Anthony Roth Costanzo (whose debut memoir Countertenor was published last month), fresh off his starring turn in Lincoln in the Bardo at the Met. The revelry continued into the night with sounds from New York City funk and soul band The Ruckus and a late-night surprise DJ set by multiple-Grammy-winning artist Ahmir Thompson, better known as Questlove, who also just so happens to be the publisher of FSG imprint AUWA Books.

And what, according to Angel, is the common denominator among the stable of scribes? “FSG writers have something important to say—and they know how to say it,” she said. “For them, the special alchemy between language and what it describes is crucial.”
